name: l10-device-types
title: Reading a device listing
spec: Monospace lines: brw-rw---- 1 root disk 8, 1 ... /dev/sda1 ; crw-rw-rw- 1 root root 1, 3 ... /dev/null ; crw-rw-rw- 1 root root 195, 0 ... /dev/nvidia0 ; prw-r--r-- ... /run/fifo ; srw-rw-rw- ... /dev/log. Callout on the first character: b block device (disks, partitions), c character device (stream of bytes: /dev/null, GPUs), p named pipe, s Unix domain socket. Callout on '8, 1': major number selects the driver (the building), minor number selects the instance (the room). Note: /proc/devices lists drivers and major numbers.
alt: How the first letter and the major and minor numbers of an ls -l line identify a device.
cap: The type letter and the major and minor numbers tell you what kind of device a file is.

name: l10-name-shift
title: Why sdX names are a trap
spec: Two columns Before and After a reboot. Before: sda, sdb, sdc. After sdb fails: sda, sdb (was sdc). Arrow from old sdc to new sdb in orange, label 'the name moved, nothing broke inside the filesystem'. Bottom green row of stable identifiers: UUID=... in fstab, /dev/mapper/vg-lv, /dev/disk/by-id (physical drive by serial), /dev/disk/by-path (slot), /dev/disk/by-uuid (recommended fstab key); GPUs by UUID from nvidia-smi -L. Paths in monospace.
anchor: ### Naming: why enumeration order is a trap
alt: Kernel disk names can shift between boots, so persistent configuration should use stable identifiers.
cap: Names like sdb depend on discovery order, so use a UUID or a /dev/disk link instead.

name: l10-driver-bind
title: Binding a device to a driver
spec: Flow: device ID (PCI vendor and device pair) then modalias then udev loads matching module then driver claims device. Side box of sysfs commands in monospace: readlink /sys/bus/pci/devices/0000:3b:00.0/driver ; ls /sys/bus/pci/drivers/nvidia. Lower row, orange illustrative swap to VFIO: unbind from current driver, set driver_override to vfio-pci, drivers_probe. Note: drain the node before any of these operations.
alt: A device is matched to a driver by its ID tables, and sysfs can unbind it and hand it to vfio-pci.
cap: Drivers claim devices by ID, and the bind and unbind files in sysfs let you swap the driver.
